answer: When rewards leave the ledger, auditors trace each payout to its exit address. Identities whose earnings sweep into the same external wallet, or into a nebula of wallets that later merge, are folded into one owner, and their rewards since the first link are clawed back from escrow. A farmer can open many keys, but each clone then needs its own exit path, funded and kept apart for good, so the garden of clones costs more to tend than it earns. Limitation: mixers can blur the inlet where coins pool, so clawback only works while rewards are still escrowed.
